title: Estate process flows
subtitle: How each governed act actually proceeds — including every way it stops
doctrine: A flow that models only the happy path documents a system nobody has. What distinguishes this estate is what it refuses, so refusals are steps here, not footnotes: each one is a real branch with a real terminal, and the build fails if a branch leads nowhere or nothing leads to it.

steps.action: Fold the governance ledger and verify its hash chain.

steps.terminal: Signing is disabled and the break is named by line. Nothing below is evidence.
Reported as a missing record, never as an empty queue — the most dangerous sentence this screen could say.

steps.action: Read why, what it rests on, what it costs, whether it reverses — all shown before any button.

steps.terminal: The proposal stays open. Nothing is authorised.

steps.action: Append proposal_signed with authorship human and the signer taken from the session, never from the request.
Append proposal_declined. Declines are kept: a register of approvals only would imply everything proposed was accepted.

steps.terminal: isAuthorised() now answers true for this proposal, and actions may cite it.
The decision is recorded and is terminal.

steps.action: POST a proposalId, title, rationale and any derivedFrom subjects.

decision.when: derivedFrom is prose, not a subject id

steps.terminal: 400. A signer decides on the why, and 'the agent suggested it' is not a why.
400 at the door, rather than a dangling parent in the lineage graph forever.
409. Never append onto a record known to be altered.

steps.action: Look the proposal up in the fold.

decision.when: open, and the content is identical

steps.terminal: 409. Re-raising a decision already made is how a queue starts asking for the same signature twice.
Nothing is written. Silence is the correct response to 'still true'.

steps.action: Append a new raised event; the fold collapses it to one queue item.
Append proposal_raised with authorship frontier, hard-coded — a request is a program, never a person.

steps.terminal: It waits in the Gov arc. Nothing else has happened.

steps.action: Raise a proposal naming the application, its source, cost and reversibility.
Decide in the Gov arc. This is the only step that can unblock the rest.

steps.terminal: acquire and place refuse and say why. There is deliberately no --force: a step that can be skipped under pressure is not a control.

steps.action: Resolve the signature, then fetch once into the content-addressed store citing it.
The source is never opened. This is the saving, not de-dup after the fact.
Stream, hash and verify before admitting the bytes; record the acquisition and a run.
Materialise a copy per machine, each placement recording the same signed proposal as its cause.
Rebuild the manual so the application becomes a feature the agent knows about.
Sweep and generate the evidence pack; the artifact, its placements and its runs all carry the signature.

steps.terminal: Installed software whose entire path — who asked, who agreed, what was fetched, where it went — is provable from the ledger.

steps.action: Name the source, and optionally the proposal that authorises the fetch.
Resolve the proposal against the governance ledger.

steps.terminal: Refused. Citing an unsigned proposal records the shape of an authorisation nobody gave, and afterwards it is indistinguishable from a real one.

steps.action: Allowed, and said out loud: this will be recorded with no authorisation and counted unprovenanced. Forcing a citation here would teach the operator to type a plausible id.
Ask whether the store already holds this hash — before opening anything.

steps.terminal: The source is never opened. Recorded as deduped and not fetched — transfer avoided, not transfer wasted.

steps.action: Hash and write in one pass at constant memory; verify before the atomic rename.

steps.terminal: The bytes never enter the store. Integrity is checked before admission, not after.
One copy held, an acquisition event, a verification event and a run — placeable on any machine without fetching again.

steps.action: Read every ledger under the store and verify each chain SEPARATELY — they cannot be concatenated.

steps.terminal: Reported as an absent record. Zero out of zero is not a clean score.

steps.action: Subjects from the failing ledger are still shown — hiding them would lose the fact that they exist — but never counted as evidence.
Read coverage first, then pick a subject.
Order the subject's events by transaction time then HLC, and fold each prefix with the system's own projector.
Walk the trail. The event's own payload is complete; the projection beside it is last-write-wins and says so.

steps.terminal: The trail stops. That is a gap in the record, not proof the subject had no origin.
Follow the declared parent and repeat, until the chain reaches a decision someone signed.

flows.name: Prove the estate to a reviewer

steps.action: Walk the store's roots and any --include paths; observe, do not judge.

steps.terminal: Refused. Numbers checked against a record we know has been altered would look authoritative and mean nothing.

steps.action: Compare disk against ledger BY PATH — a placement is judged only if its path was actually walked.

decision.when: a claimed path was not walked

steps.action: Counted as unseen — neither present nor missing — and folded into neither defect. Marking it missing would manufacture a defect out of not looking.
Build the pack: each defect measured, with the population it was measured over.

decision.when: measured zero over an empty population

steps.terminal: Reported as NOT MEASURABLE and never as clean. Exit 1.
Named as a gauge with nothing to measure. 0 of 0 and 0 of 200 are the same digit and different assurances. Exit 1.
Named individually, with the runs or objects at fault. Exit 1.
The only unqualified pass: every defect measured, zero, and with something under it. Exit 0.

steps.action: Each node probes its own services on a schedule.

steps.terminal: Nothing is written. The ledger records transitions, not observations.

steps.action: Append service_transitioned with from, to and the observer.
The collector pulls each node's own chained log and folds one board, citing the proposal that authorises the schedule.

decision.when: a pull fails or a node is stale

steps.terminal: Carried as a blind spot, never dropped. A failed pull must not make a node vanish — absence reading as health is the failure this exists to catch.
One view of the estate, with outages named and ages shown.

flows.name: Answer from the manual rather than from memory

steps.action: Generate the manual from manual.json, resolving every file, panel, endpoint and command it names.

steps.terminal: Nothing is written. The manual cannot describe something that is not there.

steps.action: Push triples to the graph, a PageIndex tree for navigation, and chunks for retrieval.

steps.terminal: Reported as PARTLY LOADED with which half failed. An agent answering confidently from a manual it never received is worse than one that says it does not know.

steps.action: Ask a question.

decision.when: anything else, and the workspace has documents

steps.terminal: Answered directly without retrieval, and marked unchecked — there are no documents to be grounded in.

steps.action: Retrieve, grade the documents, generate, then grade the answer against its sources.

steps.terminal: Returned with hallucination_check false and X-RAG-Grounded: false. The answer is not withheld; it is labelled.
An answer traceable to a section of the manual, grounded and marked as such.

flows.name: Read the estate from across the room

steps.action: Open the deck — an arc in the app, or /deck full screen on a wall.
Fold every ledger once into a single answer, so the wall cannot disagree with itself.

decision.when: no store, or the ledgers cannot be read

steps.terminal: The deck says 'not reporting' and shows nothing else. A wall of green built from a missing store is the failure this estate exists to prevent.

steps.action: Draw four figures, each with the population it was measured over, redacted while room mode is on.

decision.when: a figure changed since the last read

steps.terminal: Nothing moves. A surface that animates constantly becomes wallpaper and stops being read.

steps.action: Only the tile whose number actually changed settles, once.
Hold the key and speak.
Transcribe, then route the intent.

decision.when: asked to sign, approve or authorise

steps.terminal: The signing queue is opened and nothing is signed. A spoken instruction is not an authenticated act, and a room contains other voices.
The deck moves to the surface asked for, or answers from the ledger.
A proposal is raised with frontier authorship — it asks for a decision and takes none.
It says what it heard and what it can do, rather than guessing at a consequential verb.

steps.action: Sit still and watch. This is where the deck spends almost all of its life.
